brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Level 0 has a full base at (0,0), half bases at (1,0) and (-1,0), and bases-in-notch drawer frames; level 1 has a full base at (0,0,1) plus bases at (0,-1,1) and (0,1,1). Two storeys, checked with check_build (ok, meshClash clear).
Footprint is about 190 x 165 mm over two levels of 80 mm each; the configurator does not check the bench itself, so fit on the bench is not verified.
Two drawer units (notch stems hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf at (0,-1,0) and hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm at (0,1,0)) on the lower storey.
Hex bins: hex-bin-full-div2 (2-compartment) in level-1 cells (0,0,1), (0,-1,1), (0,1,1).

requirements.requirement: House rules (joints locked, open faces capped)
requirements.evidence: lockJoints added 4 joint bolts; capOpenFaces added solid caps on all open faces; check_build reports no issues.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex storage tower: lower storey with a central base, two half bases and two drawer notches; upper storey with three bases carrying two-compartment bins. Joints are bolted and open faces capped; check_build is clean with meshClash clear. Not verified: the tower's fit on a specific workbench, and material/load suitability for drawers.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
